invariant: Native short/int/long/size_t/integer/float/number sizes, byte order and alignment are measured. The invoked checkerror helper requires a failed protected call and the expected error pattern.

Signed and unsigned integer formats from one through sixteen bytes preserve exact endian order, sign extension and low integer bits. Extended representations reject nonzero overflow bytes; native-width limits and mixed-endian formats round-trip.
Invalid widths/options/alignment and variable-length packsize formats fail with the specified patterns. Virtual sizes near maxinteger do not allocate and overflow/too-long requests fail semantically.

Every sub-native signed and unsigned width rejects out-of-range inputs and round-trips its extrema. Native Lua min/max integers and all-one unsigned bits survive packing; native float byte order follows the measured endian branch.
Native numbers, round representable non-native float/double values and infinities survive both endian encodings; opposite-endian byte sequences reverse exactly.

Zero-terminated and counted byte strings preserve content, lengths, following fields and byte positions. Embedded zeros, too-small length fields, unfinished strings and short input raise the expected errors.
Fixed strings include zero-length fields, exact-fit copies and zero padding; oversized inputs fail. Unpack returns the correct next index after zero-terminated and fixed fields.
One mixed integer/float/number record has the size computed by packsize and unpacks the original eight values in order.

Explicit maximum alignment pads only the requested fields, including X lookahead and alignment-only records; actual bytes, sizes and unpack positions agree. Missing or invalid X followers raise expected errors.
Positive, aligned, negative and terminal empty-field positions unpack correctly; positions beyond the string fail. Terminal OK occurs after all width/alignment/position loops.

Actual pack byte order selects the native-float little/big-endian comparison. Source171 executes only on little-endian,173 only on big-endian; the other assertion is an explicit measured-inactive lexical reference.
